endorsements.quote: Ethical governance must prevent retroactive data appropriation and maintain dual protection: maternal data remain confidential unless separable from fetal data; secondary use requires independent ethical oversight.

unlisted_practices: Establish national or international repositories of fetal and perinatal data under strict governance and transparency standards, separating maternal and fetal identifiers.
Adopt deferred ownership and consent mechanisms allowing the child, once capable of discernment, to claim or manage access to their prenatal data with counselling and safeguards.
Obtain initial maternal consent that specifies potential future recontact.
Archive fetal-origin data securely under independent custodianship.
Have multidisciplinary oversight committees combining clinical, ethical, and legal expertise arbitrate requests for access to fetal data case by case.
Provide proportionate disclosure of prenatal predictive data accompanied by counselling to the child.
Establish ethical and public oversight bodies to balance individual rights and societal benefit and prevent commercial or discriminatory misuse of fetal data.
Embed fetal data repositories within existing digital-health infrastructures such as the European Health Data Space.

screen.reason: This is a brief report/commentary proposing a framework of prenatal data stewardship and addressing legal, ethical, and governance challenges around predictive fetal AI and multi-omic data.
